[tool: bash]
`/tmp/obench-cell-4q9wtkb_/bench_opencode_polyglot-rust-c_ig7jqmn0/polyglot/main.rs` now compiles and runs under both `rustc` and `g++ -x c++`. Both print the same Fibonacci numbers for the inputs I tried, with f(0) = 1 and f(1) = 1.

I tested N = 0, 1, 2, 10 and 100 with each compiler. The outputs were 1, 1, 2, 89 and 573147844013817084101. The N = 100 value is above `u64` range, so both programs add decimal digit vectors instead of using a fixed-width integer. They should therefore handle arbitrarily large N.

It works because the two compilers treat block comments differently. Rust nests `/* */` and C++ doesn't. The first line, `/* /* */`, leaves Rust inside a comment but closes the comment for C++. So C++ compiles the C++ code and Rust skips it. The C++ side then hits `#if 0`, which hides the Rust code from it. The `// */` after `#if 0` closes Rust's comment, so Rust compiles its own code. A final `/* /* */ #endif // */` hides the C++ ending from Rust, and `#endif` closes the `#if 0` for C++.
